A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Info-Gain Sampler research. All 19 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison. Remaining internal inconsistencies do not prevent matching the material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning, coding, planning, creative-writing and image-generation evaluations, together with case studies, ablations and low-step experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional comparator results in Tables 2, 3 and 5. Its appendices also retain original robustness and resource measurements.

M1.justification: The main objective and candidate-sampling cycle remain unchanged. The reported beam-search variant changes from cumulative entropy plus state uncertainty to accumulated Info-Gain plus a state score, with descending selection in Appendix D. The single-path argmin-to-argmax correction instead aligns its pseudocode with the main text's existing rule.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same math, code, Sudoku, Countdown, Alpaca-based writing, GenEval and ImageNet coverage, including the synthetic arithmetic and ultra-low-step scenarios. Added comparators do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds adapted LookUM comparisons for Dream, SDAR and TraDo in Tables 2–3. AR, previously present in the binary-judgment case study, is additionally evaluated in the full-attention reasoning comparison and creative writing in Tables 2 and 5. This substantially extends comparison against alternative decoding strategies, including another look-ahead method.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 revises the beam-ranking procedure reported for the existing fixed-budget comparison. Other stated models, metrics, temperatures, block sizes, decoding budgets and sample counts remain unchanged. Figure 8's caption changes to ImageNet-512 while its plot title still says ImageNet-256, so an actual resolution change is not established.

E4.justification: The sampler-versus-beam-versus-Best-of-N study is revised through its reported beam-scoring rule in Section 4.3 and Appendix D. Figure 4 and its conclusions remain unchanged, without establishing new measurements. The other case studies, temperature analyses, low-step tests and empirical resource analyses retain their evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report reasoning accuracy averaged over five runs and retain the same correlation statistic, p-value and percentile-distribution reporting. No new run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces many K=1 accuracy entries under unchanged reported settings: Info-Gain averages change from 60.3 to 66.2 for SDAR and from 60.3 to 68.2 for TraDo, alongside substantial baseline revisions. Tables 2, 3 and 5 add comparator results. Writing's aggregate changes from 63.1% to 62.8% because AR is included; existing pairwise scores remain unchanged. The text also corrects entropy ratios against PC-Sampler to 65.9% and 62.0%. Corrections versus reruns are not explained.

T1.justification: Appendix C aligns its conflicting definition with the main text: J changes from C−IG to IG−C, and its expected bound changes from nonnegative to nonpositive. The underlying information-gain inequality and proof are retained. Appendix F corrects beam-memory accounting to distinguish B caches from B×N candidate activations. Appendix A also changes KLASS's temporal index from t+1 to t−1 without explaining that revision.

C1.justification: The central training-free sampling contribution and broad effectiveness claims remain. The abstract and conclusion revise the reasoning headline from a 3.6% gain in full-attention evaluation to 2.9–11.6 percentage points across full-attention and semi-autoregressive settings, and revise the creative-writing headline from 63.1% to 62.8%.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.4 qualifies state uncertainty as a proxy for proximity to the training manifold. Section 4.2 newly attributes advantages over LookUM on code and planning to the immediate-cost term. Appendix C reinterprets the retained distribution as proximity to an upper bound; Appendix F replaces the claim of fewer decoding steps with explanations involving batching, caching and bypass. Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes reported code availability from forthcoming to available. Section 3.2.3 and Appendix F explain shared prefix-and-suffix dual caching; Appendix A specifies negative-entropy LookUM without SMC/NIS; Appendix D corrects pseudocode polarity and distinguishes num_steps from K. Some quantified overhead summaries are removed. Hardware and the principal hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lee et al.'s LookUM and Wei et al.'s TEAM references. It recognizes LookUM as concurrent look-ahead work and distinguishes Info-Gain through its immediate-cost term in the discussion and comparison table. This is a focused positioning extension; most related-work discussion and references are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and mechanism explanation are condensed, the conclusion is rewritten, and terminology and notation receive local corrections. Affiliations and publication front matter are updated, and a generic Impact Statement is added. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 gain comparator rows, Table 5 gains an AR column, and Table 6 gains LookUM. Table 8's cache labels and several figure captions change. Appendix figures and code listings reflow across pages. All ten figures retain identical underlying image content; there is no graphical redesign or new figure.

improvement.justification: v3 improves comparison coverage through LookUM and AR, resolves several objective/pseudocode inconsistencies, corrects entropy-ratio arithmetic and clarifies caching. These provide concrete gains in consistency and reproducibility. However, the large Table 3 replacements remain unexplained, and LookUM excludes SMC/NIS, limiting conclusions about the full comparator. The evidence supports a bounded overall improvement, rather than treating higher revised scores as proof of substantially better paper quality.
